title: Best Mattresses UK
short: Ten mattresses slept on for weeks or months, compared on comfort, support, temperature control and value, from £529 to £3,600 (double).
intro: A mattress can only be judged by sleeping on it. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' roundup of the mattresses it has tested (around 75 in all), each slept on for at least two weeks and up to three months, with standardised tests for temperature retention and firmness. Testers judged comfort and firmness, temperature control, motion isolation, the base used and value for money. Only mattresses that earned five stars on first review are included, and prices are double-size prices as reviewed.

products.name: Natural Lux Hybrid
products.best_for: Hot sleepers and allergy sufferers who want an all-natural mattress
products.key_spec: Hybrid, all-natural materials with no synthetic foam, fairly firm, 200-night trial, small single to super king
products.summary: Expert Reviews' Best Buy: a totally natural mattress, free of synthetic foam, that suits a range of sleeping positions and body weights and proved fairly firm, most comfortable on the back for the tester. Temperature regulation was excellent: in a body heat test the surface dropped from 30°C to just over 21°C in a couple of minutes. Natural materials cost more, and it can feel too firm for some, with some motion transfer.

products.name: Hybrid Mattress
products.best_for: Buyers who want good support at the lowest price
products.key_spec: Hybrid, grid-based support layer, temperature-control layer, tapered pocket springs, 200-night trial
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top pick on a budget, from a June 2024 review that earned five stars and a Recommended Award. It has just enough softness for those who like cushioning while giving the ergonomic support firm-mattress fans prefer, and neither the reviewer nor their partner felt the edge dip significantly. It has no removable cover for easy cleaning.
cons: No removable cover for ease of cleaning

products.name: Hybrid Mattress
products.best_for: Hot sleepers who want a supportive, washable-cover mattress at a mid price
products.key_spec: Hybrid, seven layers with pocket springs and bamboo-infused foam, machine-washable removable cover, 100-night trial
products.summary: Expert Reviews' September 2024 review found plenty of support right up to the edges and excellent temperature regulation: after warming the surface with a heat pad the temperature dropped from 50°C to 26.9°C in four minutes. It's a much more affordable alternative to the brand's Hybrid Bamboo Pro. It can feel too firm for some, and the removable cover is awkward to take off and refit.

products.name: Original Pro
products.best_for: Hot sleepers who want a softer, comfortable-in-any-position mattress
products.key_spec: Hybrid with ThermoSync foam layer and extra-tall 18.5cm pocket springs, vacuum-packed, 200-night trial
products.summary: Reviewed as the Emma Hybrid Thermosync in April 2025. Despite memory foam's reputation for trapping heat, it dropped from 30°C to 22.6°C in four minutes in the temperature test, and is comfortable in a range of sleeping positions. It's softer than other options but still supportive, though it may be too soft for those who prefer a firm mattress. Expert Reviews notes it's now much cheaper than at launch.
pros: Comfortable in a range of sleeping positions
cons: May be too soft for those who prefer a firm mattress

products.name: Dream Team Romsey Pocket Sprung
products.best_for: Average and heavier sleepers with back pain
products.key_spec: Pocket sprung hybrid, firm orthopaedic support, 100-night trial, 1-year warranty
products.summary: Reviewed in March 2025: the firm orthopaedic support can make a real difference to back pain. The tester said her back pain had vanished within a few days of sleeping on it on her back. Best suited to average and heavier weight sleepers, and with little foam it's also good for hot sleepers, but it may be too firm for lightweight side sleepers. Delivery to a room of your choice costs an extra £29.
pros: Orthopaedic support helps to ease aches and pains
products.search: Dreams Dream Team Romsey pocket sprung mattress

products.name: Inspired By Nature 05
products.best_for: Buyers who want a beautifully made natural mattress and can afford it
products.key_spec: Traditional pocket sprung, British wool and cotton layers, ReActivePro springs, medium firm (firm also sold), 10-year guarantee
products.summary: Reviewed in May 2026: supremely comfortable and supportive in a range of sleeping positions and one of the most comfortable mattresses the tester has slept on, with exceptional lumbar support and spinal alignment. It comes with a 10-year guarantee and a 40-night trial with exchange only. It is expensive and heavy, and delivery isn't free.
pros: Excellent levels of comfort and support
Well made, with high quality materials

products.name: Hybrid Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who want a very comfortable rolled-up mattress with cool wool layers
products.key_spec: Hybrid with wool comfort layer and microsprings, 200-night trial, single to king
products.summary: Reviewed in April 2025: one of the most comfortable bed-in-a-box mattresses tested, with a top wool layer that regulates temperature better than mattresses containing only memory foam, and extra microsprings that make it bouncy and breathable. The reviewer liked it so much they didn't want to go back to their regular mattress. It's expensive for a bed-in-a-box.

specs.Turning: Monthly for six months, then every 3 to 6 months

products.name: Premier Inn 2.0 Mattress
products.best_for: People who like a firm, deep, hotel-style mattress
products.key_spec: Pocket sprung with pillow top (polyester hollowfibre and Geltex foam), 28.5cm deep, side handles
products.summary: Reviewed in March 2025: extremely supportive, so much so the tester could lie right at the edge without feeling it would buckle, and it's the mattress the Home Editor sleeps on every night. It's almost identical to the mattresses in Premier Inn hotels and generously deep, though on the firmer side. It can't be flipped but can be rotated using the side handles.
pros: Good support, particularly at the edges
cons: May be too firm for some

products.name: Air 6.0 Memory Mattress
products.best_for: Couples or sleepers unsure of their firmness preference
products.key_spec: Hybrid memory foam, soft, medium or firm options, 40-night trial (exchange only)
products.summary: Reviewed in November 2025: despite being synthetic it dissipated heat well, dropping from 30°C to 18.7°C in a couple of minutes, and the standout benefit is the choice of soft, medium or firm. The reviewer tested the firm version, found it perfect for back sleeping and said her aches and pains disappeared overnight. Edge support could be better.
pros: Choice of soft, medium and firm feels

products.name: The Annabel Mattress
products.best_for: Buyers who want natural materials without paying premium prices
products.key_spec: Pillow top hybrid with wool, cashmere, silk and pocket springs, no trial period
products.summary: Reviewed in March 2026: a natural-materials alternative to the Hypnos when budget won't stretch, made from layers of wool, cashmere and silk over pocket springs. The reviewer found it much firmer than the 'medium firm' description suggests, but comfortable with excellent lumbar support. It has no trial period, so you can't test it at home first.
pros: Natural materials that won't break the bank

guide.q: How firm should my mattress be?
guide.a: It depends on your weight and sleeping position. Several picks here run firm: the REM-Fit, Dreams Romsey and Happy Beds Annabel suit back sleepers and heavier sleepers but may be too firm for lightweight side sleepers. The Emma Original Pro is softer, and the Slumberland Air 6.0 comes in soft, medium and firm.

guide.q: What's the best mattress for hot sleepers?
guide.a: Expert Reviews measured how quickly the surface cooled after body heat: the Slumberland dropped from 30°C to 18.7°C, the REM-Fit to just over 21°C and the Emma Original Pro to 22.6°C in four minutes. Natural fillings like wool and cotton, or little foam, as in the Dreams Romsey, also help.

guide.q: Is a home trial worth having?
guide.a: Yes, since comfort is personal. The Origin, Emma, Simba and REM-Fit all offer 200-night trials, Panda and Dreams 100 nights. Hypnos and Slumberland offer 40-night exchange-only trials, and the Happy Beds Annabel has none. Read the terms on returns carefully.

guide.q: Do I need to turn my mattress?
guide.a: It varies by model. The Origin, Panda and Emma here need no turning, the REM-Fit should be rotated every three months, and the Simba more often for the first six months. Pillow-top mattresses like the Silentnight can't be flipped but can be rotated to even out wear.
